name: R1LP0108ESF-5SI#S1
title: R1LP0108E series: 1 Mbit (128K × 8) low-power asynchronous SRAM, 5 V, 55 ns
summary: A 1 Mbit static RAM organised as 131,072 bytes, built with 0.15 µm CMOS and TFT technology, running from a single 4.5 V to 5.5 V supply. Seventeen address lines, eight three-state data lines, two chip selects of opposite sense (CS1# and CS2), OE# and WE# form a plain asynchronous interface with TTL-level inputs and outputs, no clock and no refresh. Standby current is 0.6 µA typical at 5 V and 25 °C, and contents hold down to 2.0 V, and the series is aimed at battery-operated and battery-backed memory. All six orderable parts are 55 ns, −40 to +85 °C, in a 525-mil 32-pin SOP (ESN), an 8 × 13.4 mm 32-pin sTSOP (ESA) or an 8 × 20 mm 32-pin TSOP (ESF); R1LP0108ESF-5SI#S1 is the TSOP on embossed tape.
key_figures: 25 mA typ, 35 mA max at minimum cycle
0.6 µA typ at 25 °C; 10 µA max to +85 °C
32-pin SOP (525 mil), 32-pin sTSOP (8 × 13.4 mm), 32-pin TSOP (8 × 20 mm)

operation.text: Asynchronous CMOS static RAM holding 131,072 bytes (1,048,576 bits) behind seventeen address lines and one common eight-bit data bus that carries both input and output. It needs no clock and no refresh, runs from one supply of 4.5 V to 5.5 V, and its inputs and outputs work at TTL levels.

The chip is selected only with CS1# low and CS2 high; CS1# high or CS2 low puts it in standby with the data lines at high impedance whatever WE# and OE# do. The two selects of opposite sense ease memory expansion, and the three-state outputs can be wired together with other devices. OE# keeps the outputs off so the part does not fight another driver on the bus; with the chip selected, WE# high and OE# high, the outputs are disabled.

With TTL levels on the selects (CS2 at VIL, or CS2 and CS1# both at VIH) the standby current is at most 3 mA. With CMOS levels (CS2 at 0.2 V or less, or CS1# and CS2 both within 0.2 V of Vcc) it falls to ISB1: 0.6 µA typical at 5 V and 25 °C, and at most 2, 3, 8 or 10 µA up to 25, 40, 70 or 85 °C.

A read runs with WE# held high. Data is valid tAA after the address settles, tACS1 after CS1# falls, tACS2 after CS2 rises and tOE after OE# falls, whichever comes last; the outputs leave high impedance tCLZ1, tCLZ2 or tOLZ after the matching edge. Once the address changes, the old data stays for tOH. The outputs float again within tCHZ1, tCHZ2 or tOHZ after the chip is deselected or OE# rises.

The selects are held active and WE# pulses low for at least tWP. The address is set up tAS before WE# falls and held tWR after it rises; tAW counts from a valid address and tCW from the selects to the end of the write. Data must be on DQ for tDW before WE# rises and stay tDH after. With OE# low the outputs float within tWHZ after WE# falls; OE# rising floats them within tOHZ. After the write they drive again tOW after WE# rises, or tOLZ after OE# falls.

WE# goes low first and the write is timed by CS1# falling and CS2 rising for at least tCW, with OE# held high. The address leads the select edges by tAS and is held tWR after them; data is set up tDW before the selects end the write and held tDH after.

Contents are kept with Vcc as low as VDR = 2.0 V while the chip is held deselected at CMOS levels, by CS1# at Vcc-0.2V or above (with CS2 at Vcc-0.2V or above or at 0.2 V or below) or by CS2 between 0 V and 0.2 V. The select goes inactive at least tCDR before Vcc drops below 4.5 V and stays inactive for tR (5 ms minimum) after Vcc is back above 4.5 V. Outside the retention window the CS1# high level is referenced at 2.2 V and the CS2 low level at 0.2 V. At Vcc = 3.0 V the retention current is 0.6 µA typical at 25 °C and at most 10 µA up to 85 °C.
